title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
This is page 2 of a letter from Grothendieck to Lipman Bers (Les Aumettes, 15.4.1984), written in the context of his microseminar with Y. Ladegaillerie.

**Setting.** Fix a reference surface X_0 of genus g with ν holes, with 2g-2+ν>0 and d = 3g-3+ν. Two spaces are compared:
- T_{g,ν} =: M̃_{g,ν}, the Teichmüller space of ν-pointed algebraic curves. It is homeomorphic to C^d.
- MB̃_{g,ν}, the Teichmüller space of compact bordered Riemann surfaces. Through the canonical hyperbolic metric with geodesic boundary, it is homeomorphic to C^d × (R_{>0})^ν, the extra factor being the boundary lengths ℓ_i.

**The enlarged space.** Grothendieck enlarges MB̃ by allowing 'generalized boundary': a boundary component may degenerate to a point (a puncture or cusp, ℓ_i = 0). This gives a manifold with corners MB̃_{g,ν} ≅ C^d × (R_{≥0})^ν. M̃_{g,ν} sits inside it as the deepest corner stratum (all ℓ_i = 0). In modern terms, this is the family of Teichmüller spaces T_{g,ν}(L), L ∈ R_{≥0}^ν, familiar from Mirzakhani's work.

**The problem.** He wants an intrinsic, mapping-class-group-equivariant retraction MB̃ → M̃ with fibres (R_{≥0})^ν. More precisely, he wants a natural action of the multiplicative semigroup (R_{≥0})^I on MB̃ with three properties:
- the subgroup (R_{>0})^I acts freely on the interior MB̃°;
- M̃ is the quotient;
- each fibre F becomes an (R_{≥0})^I-torsor-like object once an origin in F ∩ MB̃° is chosen.

**Naive version and his doubt.** In Fenchel–Nielsen coordinates for a pants decomposition, the obvious candidate scales the boundary lengths ℓ_i by λ_i and keeps the other coordinates fixed. He doubts this is intrinsic, i.e. independent of the pants decomposition.

**Geometric construction.** He proposes 'hyperbolic surgery' instead. Cap each genuine boundary circle with the cone on that circle. The cone is conformally a disc, using the Riemannian (arclength) structure of the geodesic circle; the gluing is well defined because it is unique up to a rotation, which is a disc automorphism. The result is a compact Riemann surface without boundary, with ν marked points. Passing to rigidified isomorphism classes gives the retraction MB̃ → M̃.

The next page refines this. The capped surface also carries a system of disjoint 'admissible' discs around the points. Admissibility means the circle action on each boundary circle coming from the disc equals the one coming from the hyperbolic geodesic boundary. The disc radii, viewed as discs in the tangent spaces T_{s_i}, form R_{>0}-torsors (hermitian metrics on T_{s_i} up to scale). The intended fibre parameters are therefore metrics on the tangent lines at the marked points, i.e. on the duals of the ψ-class line bundles L_i.
errors: The statement that the fibres are homeomorphic to (R^+)^ν, and that the capping map coincides with a semigroup-orbit structure, is asserted and expected rather than proved. Surjectivity and injectivity of the capping map onto the space of admissible disc systems is exactly the open 'pants problem' he submits to Bers.

Grothendieck's suspicion is justified: scaling boundary lengths in Fenchel–Nielsen coordinates is generally not intrinsic. Change-of-pants transition maps depend on the boundary lengths, so the naive action is not mapping-class-group equivariant. No error, but the 'computationally obvious' action cannot serve as the definition.
A minor terminology slip: 'variety with boundary' in the topological sense actually means a manifold with corners.

ideas.what: Moduli/Teichmüller space of bordered hyperbolic surfaces with boundary lengths allowed to be zero (cusps), forming a manifold with corners containing T_{g,ν} as the ℓ=0 stratum
ideas.modern_name: Family T_{g,n}(L), L∈R_{≥0}^n, of Teichmüller spaces of surfaces with geodesic boundary of prescribed lengths
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in hyperbolic geometry (Fenchel–Nielsen, Thurston); systematic use by Mirzakhani (2007), Mondello, Do–Norbury
ideas.where_published: Possibly echoed in Esquisse d'un programme's remarks on Teichmüller towers and surgery of surfaces; no explicit treatment known

ideas.what: Intrinsic, mapping-class-group-equivariant retraction of bordered Teichmüller space onto punctured Teichmüller space, via conformal capping of geodesic boundary circles by cones/discs
ideas.modern_name: Capping/sewing discs onto parametrized boundary (Segal-type sewing); relation between surfaces with boundary and punctured surfaces with local data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Segal (CFT, c.1987), Friedan–Shenker, Vafa; Huang (vertex operator algebras) for punctured surfaces with local coordinates

ideas.what: Semigroup (R_{≥0})^I acting on MB̃ with M̃ as quotient, and fibres as (R_{>0})^I-torsors identified (next page) with radii of discs in the tangent spaces T_{s_i}
ideas.modern_name: Torsor/fibration of hermitian metrics on the tangent lines at marked points (unit circle bundles of the ψ-class line bundles L_i); analogue of Penner's decorated Teichmüller space T×R_{>0}^n
ideas.usually_credited_to: Penner (decorated Teichmüller space, 1987); Mirzakhani (2007), relating boundary-length moduli to ψ-classes via circle bundles

missed.claim: Grothendieck relates the boundary-length deformation of bordered hyperbolic surfaces to R_{>0}-torsors of metrics on the tangent spaces at the marked points of the limiting punctured curve. Modern language: L ∈ R_{≥0}^ν deformations ↔ the circle/metric bundles of the ψ-class line bundles. This is the same geometric link that underlies Mirzakhani's 2007 proof that Weil–Petersson volumes V_{g,n}(L) are polynomials whose top coefficients are ψ-intersection numbers. He formulates it as an intrinsic fibration problem three decades before Mirzakhani, but without any symplectic or volume content.
missed.quote: I expect the semi-group (R^+)^I ... to act on MB̃ in a natural way, with free action of the subgroup (R^{+*})^ν upon MB̃° , in such a way that M̃ is just the quotient
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an early, intrinsic, non-symplectic formulation of the T(L) → T(0) comparison. The question of a canonical mapping-class-group-equivariant identification (not just a homeomorphism) remains interesting, e.g. for Mirzakhani-type recursions or for hyperbolic versus conformal 'grafting' comparisons.

missed.claim: The intrinsic definition of the semigroup action, and the proof that the conformal-capping map gives a retraction with (R_{≥0})^ν fibres, are posed as an open problem to Bers and not resolved here.
missed.quote: it is not clear that this operation is intrinsic - and if it were intrinsic, an intrinsic geometric description would still be desired.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A canonical equivariant fibration of T_{g,n}(L) over T_{g,n} given by capping is not, as far as I know, a standard result. Settling it would clarify the relation between bordered and punctured moduli used in topological recursion.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a hitherto unpublished letter to Bers with a clear, prescient formulation: bordered surfaces with lengths in R_{≥0}, an intrinsic retraction by conformal capping, and fibres as torsors of tangent-space metrics (ψ-bundles). It anticipates structures later central in Penner, Segal and Mirzakhani, but the mathematics is conjectural and the individual ingredients are now standard.
transcription_corrections: Line 4: the image shows '(R̲^{*})^ν' with the asterisk overstruck; the intended reading is (R̲^+)^ν with R_{≥0}, as the transcription gives.
'the fibers being homeomorphic to (R̲^+)^ν' — in the image the exponent ν appears overwritten with I, i.e. (R̲^+)^I.
'by_F the action' — the handwritten F is an insertion belonging to 'F fiber F' / 'F∩MB̃°'; the reading 'by the action' is correct.
'computatinally' is typed 'computationally' with a typo in the original; harmless.
